title: Air India 171
summary: Air India Flight 171, a Boeing 787-8 flying from Ahmedabad to London Gatwick, crashed 32 seconds after takeoff on 12 June 2025 into a medical college hostel near the airport, killing 241 of 242 occupants and 19 people on the ground. The AAIB's preliminary report found the front flight recorder showed both engines lost thrust after their fuel control switches moved from RUN to CUTOFF three seconds after liftoff; the reason for the switch movement had not been established.

The aircraft began to lose altitude and crashed into the hostel block of the B. J. Medical College campus 0.9 nmi from the runway.
Several college buildings were severely damaged by the impact and subsequent fire, including student accommodation and the resident doctors' hostel.

events.text: The Boeing 787-8 lifted off from runway 23 at Ahmedabad at 13:38:39 IST after a 62-second takeoff roll, with light winds of 6 knots and visibility of 6 km.

The aircraft reached a maximum pressure altitude of around 625 ft and a maximum airspeed of 180 knots before it began to lose altitude.
After 32 seconds of flight the aircraft crashed into the hostel block of B. J. Medical College 0.9 nmi from the runway, its tail striking the campus canteen roof before it broke apart.
The wreckage and subsequent fire severely damaged five buildings including the student and resident doctors' hostels, and only one of the 242 occupants survived.

notes: Preliminary AAIB report only; the reason the fuel control switches moved to CUTOFF had not been determined at time of writing.
